tech.text: Tech Tower is the Lettie Pate Whitehead Evans Administration Building. Completed in 1888, it was designed by Bruce and Morgan in the Romanesque Revival style. Its historical roles included teaching and administration.

clough.text: The G. Wayne Clough Undergraduate Learning Commons opened for the fall 2011 semester. It honors former Georgia Tech president G. Wayne Clough and adjoins Price Gilbert Library. It supports undergraduate learning.

kendeda.text: The Kendeda Building for Innovative Sustainable Design reached substantial completion and soft launch in fall 2019. Classes began in January 2020; Living Building Challenge certification followed in March 2021. Lord Aeck Sargent and The Miller Hull Partnership led architecture; Skanska USA built it.

campanile.text: The Kessler Campanile is an 80-foot stainless-steel landmark designed by Richard Hill. It was constructed for the 1996 Olympics and stands between the John Lewis Student Center and Tech Green.

klaus.text: The Klaus Advanced Computing Building officially opened with a ribbon-cutting on October 26, 2006. A gift from Christopher Klaus made it possible. It supports computing research, including robotics, supercomputing and information security.

brittain.text: Brittain Dining Hall was originally constructed in 1928. Its 2026 reopening followed a two-year renovation. Collegiate Gothic features in its exterior and main dining room were retained while kitchens, service areas and systems were modernized.

mccamish.text: McCamish Pavilion is Georgia Tech's basketball arena, named for Hank McCamish. Its first men's game was November 9, 2012 against Tulane. It occupies the former Alexander Memorial Coliseum site at 10th and Fowler Streets. The renovation included a rectangular seating bowl and upper deck.

carnegie.text: The Carnegie Building was built in 1907 as Georgia Tech's first purpose-built library.

towers.text: Tech Square 3 is named George Tower | Scheller Tower. Its first three floors were scheduled to open January 12, 2026. The 14-story Scheller Tower houses graduate and executive business programs; the 18-story George Tower houses the H. Milton Stewart School of Industrial and Systems Engineering.
